speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. Have these symptoms been present for a long time, or did they start suddenly? Also, do you experience any trouble swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Can you tell me if your symptoms have fluctuated throughout the day over the past few weeks? Also, do you have a history of thyroid disease or myasthenia gravis?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Routine blood work including Creatine Kinase (CK), Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), and Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
